![](/assets/software/pycse.svg){width=160 fig-align="center" fig-alt="pycse logo"}

[pycse](https://github.com/jkitchin/pycse) 2.12.0 is on PyPI. This is a bigger
release than usual, and a few of the changes will alter results or break existing
code, so it is worth reading the first section before upgrading.

```bash
pip install --upgrade pycse
```

## Changes that may affect your code

pycse now requires Python 3.12 or newer, and the JAX stack moves up to `jax>=0.10`,
`flax>=0.12.7` and `optax>=0.2.5`.

Prediction intervals from `predict()` and `polyval()` now have shape `(n, 2)`
instead of `(2, n)`, the same as `nlpredict()` has always returned. Column 0 is the
lower bound and column 1 the upper bound. If you unpack the intervals, the fix is
one transpose:

```python
y, yint, se = predict(X, y, pars, XX)
lower, upper = yint.T    # was: lower, upper = yint
```

The `optimizer="bfgs"` and `"lbfgs"` options in the JAX models (`DPOSE`, `KAN`,
`KANLLPR`, `KfoldNN` and `SISSOEnsemble`) now run a real L-BFGS with a line search
from optax. Before, they ran Adam with a cosine schedule. Your fits will be
different, and they should actually be converged now. If you need the old
behavior, use `optimizer="adam_cosine"`.

`JAXMonotonicRegressor` is now only monotone by default. It used to be convex as
well, which meant concave or S-shaped monotone data could not be fitted. Pass
`convexity="convex"` to get the old behavior, or `convexity="concave"` for the
other case.

## What is new

The largest addition is `pycse.sklearn.zenn`, an independent JAX/Flax
implementation of Zentropy-Enhanced Neural Networks from Wang, Shang, Liu and Hao,
"[ZENN: A thermodynamics-inspired computational framework for heterogeneous
data-driven modeling](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2511227122)," *PNAS* 123(1),
e2511227122 (2026). It provides `ZENNRegressor`,
`ZENNRegressorNLL` and `ZENNClassifier`. Like the other models in
`pycse.sklearn`, they follow the scikit-learn estimator API.

`LeafModelRegressor(refine_splits=True)` chooses each split threshold for the leaf
model instead of for constant leaves, so the breakpoints land in the right place
for piecewise-linear data. The active learning tools picked up a `penalty_scale`
option for penalized batches, and `ActiveSurrogate.build()` and `LatinSquare` take a
`random_state` so results are reproducible.

The MCP server works with both the 1.x and 2.x versions of `mcp`, and the Claude
Code skill installed by `pycse skill install` was rewritten. It now covers the
regression functions, all of the sklearn models, design of experiments and active
learning.

## Fixes

`pycse.__version__` finally reports the installed version. `nlpredict()` works
for a single prediction point, `NNGMM` works on Python 3.12, and `NNBR` reports
the correct standard deviation of the intercept. In active learning, penalized
batches no longer contain duplicate points and `ThompsonSampling` makes a new
draw on every call. The hashcache backends return NumPy arrays and tuples with
their original types, and `pycse.sklearn` now imports its models lazily, so
`import pycse.sklearn` no longer loads every backend.

The full list is in the
[changelog](https://github.com/jkitchin/pycse/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md). As
always, issues and pull requests are welcome on
[GitHub](https://github.com/jkitchin/pycse).
